theorem: A positive integer k is the half-length of some canonical C041 long-form word if and only if k=k(w,m)=3+w+bit_length(m)+ceil(3m(w+1)/2) for some integers w>=1,m>=1.
For fixed w, k(w,m+1)-k(w,m)>=3 for every m>=1. Therefore two consecutive supported half-lengths k and k+1 can never be realized with the same variable-bitlength w.

The first syntactically supported consecutive pair after the unsupported integer 14 is 15,16: k(1,3)=15 and k(2,2)=k(4,1)=16. This identifies only a syntax-level next discriminator; H_15 nonemptiness and H_15 intersection P_16 are not decided here.
proof: The frozen encoder contributes 8 MAGIC bits, gamma(v) length 2w-1, gamma(m) length 2b-1, and 3m literals of width w+1. Thus B=8+(2w-1)+(2b-1)+3m(w+1)=6+2w+2b+3m(w+1).
Only a trailing zero may be added to make the word even, so k=ceil(B/2)=3+w+b+ceil(3m(w+1)/2).

Conversely, for every w>=1 and m>=1 choose v=2^(w-1) and any valid nonempty 3CNF with m clauses using variable 1. The frozen encoder accepts it canonically, so every displayed arithmetic support point is realized.

Fix w and set q=w+1. If q is even, ceil(3mq/2)=3mq/2 and successive m increase k by 3q/2>=3, apart from a nonnegative bit_length(m) jump. If q is odd, then w is even and q>=3; with a=3q odd, ceil(a(m+1)/2)-ceil(am/2) alternates between (a-1)/2 and (a+1)/2, whose minimum is at least 4. Again bit_length(m) can only add 0 or 1. Hence the fixed-w gap is always at least 3.

For a fixed bit-length cell b, if w is odd the support values form an arithmetic progression of step 3(w+1)/2. If w is even, the even-m and odd-m subsequences are arithmetic progressions of step 3(w+1), offset by (3(w+1)+1)/2. This is an exact representation of the support spectrum, not a density or asymptotic completeness claim.
